content_voiceover: K M T two A rearranged ALL, formerly known as M L L rearranged, is one of the highest-risk subtypes in pediatric ALL, and this slide focuses specifically on the non-infant population, since infant K M T two A ALL is generally discussed separately. Among non-infant cases, t four, eleven, q twenty-one, q twenty-three, producing the K M T two A colon colon A F F one fusion, had the worst event-free survival of any K M T two A partner, so if you see this specific translocation on boards, flag it as particularly high risk. As with most high-risk ALL subtypes, minimal residual disease at the end of induction was the single most important prognostic factor, and this held true both for K M T two A colon colon A F F one ALL and for K M T two A rearranged T-cell ALL, reinforcing that M R D response trumps genotype alone when predicting outcome. Finally, and this is a somewhat counterintuitive but important point, allogeneic stem cell transplant failed to improve outcomes for K M T two A colon colon A F F one ALL in this data, which challenges the older assumption that transplant automatically benefits every high-risk genetic subtype, and pushes the field toward finding better targeted approaches, like menin inhibitors, rather than relying on transplant alone.
keypoints: Non-infant t(4;11)(q21;q23), KMT2A::AFF1, has the worst EFS among KMT2A subtypes
End-of-induction MRD is the strongest prognostic factor in KMT2A::AFF1 and KMT2A-rearranged T-ALL
Allogeneic transplant did not improve outcomes in KMT2A::AFF1 ALL
Highlights the need for targeted approaches beyond transplant in this high-risk subtype
keypoint_voiceover: Non-infant K M T two A colon colon A F F one ALL, from t four eleven, carries the worst outcomes among K M T two A subtypes, end-of-induction M R D is the key prognostic factor, and notably, allogeneic transplant failed to improve outcomes in this group.
